agnostic_oa_w2136226659_normality_transf.interpretation: Source fact: the Betti representation space is the fiber of the single surface relation in GL(n)^{2g}, giving a component-dimension lower bound. Irreducible representations form a smooth locus of the expected dimension. Reducible representations are covered by conjugates of block parabolics; induction on the diagonal ranks and cohomology of the off-diagonal block bound this locus, showing that every component meets the irreducible locus and that the singular locus has codimension at least two, including a direct tangent calculation in the exceptional case. Being a complete intersection supplies Cohen–Macaulay S2, while codimension-one smoothness supplies R1, hence normality by Serre. Isosingularity transfers normality to de Rham and Dolbeault representation spaces, and invariant-ring quotients preserve it for coarse moduli. Interpretive inference: normality is obtained by isolating the only plausible bad locus through representation type, proving it too small to affect codimension one, and then using local-model equivalence instead of repeating the singularity analysis in every realization.
